detail.differences: In CS2, if you use Push-to-Talk in external apps or saw audio hitches on key press, Steam also exposes Streamlined Push To Talk; unlike VALORANT, CS2 does not split Team vs Party voice bindings.
Physical 360° match does NOT mean identical visual feel: default 16:9 horizontal FOV differs (103° in VALORANT vs ~106.26° in CS2), and weapon ADS vs CS2 AWP/Scout zoom multipliers scale differently.
CS2 queues Video changes behind an explicit Apply Changes step inside Advanced Video, while VALORANT saves Video options immediately.

detail.safetyNote: Do not blindly copy keybinds across games — map only the grenade binds whose ergonomics match your hand comfort.

turns.message: What CS2 sensitivity matches my VALORANT sensitivity?
turns.fallbackReason: Fallback mode is selected in the research controls.
turns.reply: Hipfire Mouse Sensitivity (360° Distance) (Similar function with differences): Both games expose raw yaw-based hipfire sensitivity sliders. Under default yaw scaling (VALORANT 0.07 deg/count vs CS2 m_yaw 0.022 deg/count), multiplying VALORANT hipfire sensitivity by 0.07 / 0.022 (≈ 3.1818) matches physical mouse distance for a 360° turn. 360° starting point (VALORANT -> CS2): 0.4 × (0.07 / 0.022) ≈ 1.27. Matches physical 360° hipfire turn distance — NOT identical screen-space speed because horizontal FOV differs (VALORANT 103° vs CS2 ~106.26° at 16:9).

turns.message: How does Global Shadow Quality differ from Dynamic Shadows?
turns.reply: Global Shadow Quality adjusts how shadows look. Dynamic Shadows controls which light sources produce shadows for moving objects such as players. Sun Only can reduce graphics work, but fewer indoor player shadows can remove a useful visibility cue.

explanations.label: Global Shadow Quality
explanations.path: Video > Advanced Video > Presets > Global Shadow Quality
explanations.explanation: Sets the overall quality of shadows.
explanations.catalogDescription: Sets the overall quality of shadows.
explanations.tradeoffs: Higher shadow quality generally costs more GPU time; the exact effect is hardware dependent.

turns.message: What is the difference between FPS and monitor refresh rate?
turns.reply: FPS counts how many frames the game renders per second. Refresh rate, in hertz, counts how many times the display can update per second. A 240 Hz monitor can refresh 240 times per second. The frame rate the game produces still depends on the scene, hardware and settings.
